turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic? What's been concerning you?
turns.patient_response:
I guess... I guess they brought me in because of the warehouse. I work freight, moving stock around. We get a lot of corrugated cardboard. Did you know there's a difference between regular cardboard and corrugated fiberboard? I learned about materials a bit in college before I left to start working. The fiberboard has that wavy layer inside so it can hold more weight. 

But yeah, at work, I keep doing things... like, I'll just freeze. I just stop and hold my arms up in the air right by the forklift. And I copy the beeping sounds it makes when it backs up, and the hand signals the drivers use. The drivers are always drinking those huge energy drinks, the green cans. I don't like the green ones, they taste weird, kind of like copper or battery acid. 

But I also started moving the boxes in these strange little patterns. I just arrange them in the patterns, even when everyone is yelling for me to stop. My supervisor yells a lot. He has this really loud voice, kind of like my uncle does when he watches football on Thanksgiving... he always gets so mad at the TV... but yeah, they brought me here because of the boxes and the freezing, I think.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, wandering off-topic to discuss cardboard types, energy drinks, and their uncle watching football before returning to the main point.
symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient describes freezing with arms up (posturing), copying beeping sounds and hand signals (echolalia and echopraxia), and arranging boxes in strange patterns (stereotypy).

turns.doctor_question: When you taste that copper or battery acid flavor in the green energy drinks, or when you hear the forklift beeping — are these things actually happening around you, or do you sometimes experience these tastes and sounds when nothing is there?
turns.patient_response:
No, I mean... the forklift is definitely right there. It's real. I hear it because it's backing up in aisle four. Aisle four is where they put all the heavy pallets. And the energy drinks, I only taste that if I actually take a sip from someone's can. I don't just taste it out of nowhere. 

The cans are aluminum, but the taste is... yeah, like copper. Copper is a really good conductor of electricity, actually. I learned about that in my physics class before I stopped going. That's why they use it in all the house wiring instead of other metals. My dad tried to rewire our kitchen light once and he blew the main circuit breaker. Sparks went everywhere, it was really bright. We had to eat cold sandwiches for like three days because the fridge got completely shut off and all the meat was going bad. I like turkey sandwiches okay, but only if the bread isn't soggy. When the tomatoes sit on the bread for too long in the lunchbox, it gets all mushy, and I just can't stand the texture of mushy bread. It feels wrong on my teeth.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, drifting from the taste of copper to electrical wiring, a blown circuit breaker, eating cold sandwiches, and the texture of mushy bread.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies experiencing the tastes or sounds when nothing is there, stating the forklift is real and they only taste the drink when taking a sip.

turns.doctor_question: You mentioned freezing and copying the forklift sounds and hand signals — when you do these things, are you aware that you're doing them, or do you sometimes find yourself doing them without realizing it?
turns.patient_response: I'm not really sure... I don't know if I realize it right when it happens. I know I do the hand signals, but... hand signals are super important, you know? Like if your turn signal breaks on your car. My buddy had this old Honda Civic, and the left blinker just completely died on him. We were driving down to the lake and he had to stick his arm out the window every time we turned. It was so hot that day, and his AC was totally busted too. We had to stop at this gas station to get ice cream just to cool down, but it melted all over my hands before we even got back to the car. I usually get strawberry, but they only had vanilla. Vanilla is kind of boring, it's like... the default flavor. It's like the regular flat cardboard of ice cream, just plain. But yeah, with the freezing at the warehouse... I don't really know. I just do it, I guess.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech demonstrates tangentiality and derailment, wandering from the topic of hand signals to a friend's broken car blinker, a trip to the lake, and ice cream flavors.
symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient acknowledges engaging in abnormal motor behaviors, specifically freezing and copying hand signals at the warehouse.

turns.doctor_question: When you freeze up and do those hand signals and copying sounds at work, can you stop yourself if you really try to, or does it feel like something you can't control even if you wanted to stop?
turns.patient_response:
I mean... I don't really think I can stop. Like I was saying before, I just find myself doing it... freezing with my arms up by the forklift, making the beeping noises and the signals, or putting the boxes into those strange little patterns. Even when everyone is standing right there yelling at me to stop, I just keep doing it. I don't know if I can control it. 

My supervisor yells so loud, it echoes off the corrugated metal roof. Metal roofs are crazy loud when it rains, actually. We had a tin roof on a shed growing up, and during a storm it sounded like a massive drum solo. My friend tried to learn the drums back in high school, but his parents made him put the drum kit out in the unheated garage because the cymbals gave his mom terrible migraines. Migraines sound awful, like your vision gets all blurry and your whole head pulses. I don't really get headaches much, mostly I just get thirsty from all the dust at work. The cardboard dust gets everywhere, it coats your throat and makes you cough. But yeah... with the freezing and the boxes... I don't think I can stop it. It just happens.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech exhibits tangentiality and loose associations, drifting from their supervisor yelling to metal roofs, rain, drums, and migraines before returning to the topic.
symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient confirms they cannot control their abnormal motor behaviors, such as freezing with arms up, making beeping noises, and arranging boxes in strange patterns.

turns.doctor_question: How long have you been experiencing these freezing episodes, the copying of sounds and hand signals, and the unusual box patterns at work? Has this been going on for just a few days or weeks, or has it been happening for several months or longer?
turns.patient_response: I guess... it's been about six months now? Yeah, the weird stuff at the warehouse, the talking and the freezing up and everything... it's been going on for like six months. Six months is exactly half a year, which is how long I had to wait to get my driver's license after I failed the written test the first time. I didn't study the section on right-of-way at four-way stops because I thought it was obvious, but they try to trick you with the wording on those tests. The DMV is always so crowded, too. You have to take a little paper ticket with a number on it and just sit in those hard plastic chairs for hours. The chairs are always that weird shade of blue, like... hospital blue, you know? It's the same color as the scrubs the nurses wear when you go in for a flu shot. I hate needles, they make my stomach feel all tight and weird. But yeah, it's been about six months at work with all that stuff happening.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, drifting from answering about the duration of their symptoms into a lengthy, unrelated tangent about the DMV, blue chairs, and needles.
symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient confirms experiencing 'the freezing up' and other 'weird stuff' at work, acknowledging the disorganized and abnormal behaviors (like freezing and copying sounds) mentioned by the doctor.

I don't know how he didn't sweat to death. Sweating makes my skin itch, especially under my work shirt. But yeah, no... no special meanings to the patterns or anything like that.
